summary: Automate Slack channel and Confluence space provisioning when a new Jira internal-support project is created
description:
Issue summary:
We currently provision Slack channels and Confluence spaces for new internal-support Jira projects manually. This task requests an automated workflow so that when an internal-support Jira project is created, a corresponding Slack channel, Confluence space, and JIRA project-level permissions template are created automatically and wired to the correct owner groups.

Background / Why: 
- Manual provisioning is error-prone and inconsistent (naming conventions, missing archetypes, wrong permissions).
- Multiple recent onboarding requests required manual follow-ups (time wasted for Platform and IT).
- We want a standardized lifecycle: create -> archive policy -> decommission hook tied to Jira project status.

Impact: 
- Reduces onboarding time by ~30–60 minutes per new project.
- Ensures access control is consistent and audited.
- Prevents stale channels/spaces from lingering when projects are closed.

Requirements / Acceptance criteria: 
1) When a new Jira project is created under project key prefix INT-, automation creates:
   - Slack channel following naming convention: #int-<project-key>-<short-name>
   - Confluence space titled: "INT - <Project Full Name>" with a space key like INT<NNNN> or other deterministic mapping
   - Applies the internal-support permission template to the Confluence space (editors: internal-support-admins, viewers: company-wide where appropriate)
   - Populates the Slack channel purpose and topic with links to the Jira project and Confluence space
2) Owner and admin groups are assigned from the Jira project lead mapping (e.g., jira:lead -> slack:channel-admins, confluence:space-admins)
3) Automated onboarding message posted to the new Slack channel with checklist and links
4) When Jira project is set to Archived/Closed, the automation:
   - Changes Slack channel to read-only and posts decommission notice
   - Flags Confluence space with a "to be archived" label and notifies space admins
5) All actions are logged in a central audit log (Confluence page or a designated S3 bucket) with timestamp, actor, and correlation IDs
6) Admin UI/CLI for manually re-running provisioning for an existing Jira project must be provided

Proposed approach / implementation notes: 
- Use platform-automation repo (existing playbooks) and Jira webhooks to notify a new provisioning service.
- Slack creation via workspace admin token with channel name validation and rate-limiting.
- Confluence space creation using API with templated home page from the "Internal Support" template.
- Store mapping of Jira project key -> Slack channel -> Confluence space in a small DynamoDB table (or Postgres) with TTL for audit entries.
- Use short-lived service accounts and pre-approved OAuth scopes; surface the required scopes in a separate PR.

Security / Permissions considerations: 
- Provisioner must run as a dedicated automation service account with least privilege.
- Any admin tokens must be rotated and stored in KMS.
- Ensure created Confluence spaces are not public by default unless explicitly requested.
- Slack channel creation should respect global allowed prefixes and disallowed words list.

Rollback / Failure modes: 
- If Confluence creation fails after Slack channel creation, automation should roll back Slack channel (archive + annotate) and create a Jira comment with failure details and runbook link.
- Retries should be idempotent and safe for partial runs.

Operational runbook pointers: 
- On failures, notify #platform-automation and create a ticket with correlation id.
- Provide a dashboard in the Console showing provisioning success/failure rates and latency.

Timeline / Phasing suggestion: 
- Phase 1 (MVP, 2 weeks): Jira webhook -> Slack creation + message + basic logging. Manual Confluence step via CLI.
- Phase 2 (next 2–3 weeks): Full Confluence integration + permissions mapping + archive hooks.
- Phase 3: Audit dashboard, manual re-run UI, and onboarding analytics.
